transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main thing is I haven’t really been eating right. For the last few weeks my appetite’s just been kind of gone. Like after a shift I’ll usually grab something I like, you know, and lately it just sits there. I take a few bites because I know I should, but I’m kind of forcing it.

It’s weird, because I used to look forward to that, especially after standing around all night watching monitors and people doing the same dumb stuff at the casino… but yeah, sorry. That’s mostly why I came in.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I think so. Most days it’s like I’m carrying around this heavy, flat feeling. I’ll be home with my family, or sitting in the break room at work with the guys talking about whatever game’s on, and I’m there, but I’m not really there, if that makes sense.

Like everybody’s moving around normal and I’m just kind of… behind glass or something. I don’t know. It’s not like I’m crying all the time, it’s more just this low, dull thing that follows me around.
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Yeah… yeah, I have. I mean, I used to actually look forward to stuff, like going for a run in the morning, messing around on guitar, cooking dinner… nothing big, just normal stuff.

Lately I keep skipping it. I’ll tell myself I’m gonna run, and then I just don’t. Or I pick up the guitar and it feels like… I don’t know, like another task. Same with cooking. I used to like making dinner, even if it was just something simple, and now it’s like this chore I can’t make myself care about.

Which is stupid, because I used to complain I didn’t have enough time for those things with work and everything, and now when I do have time I just kind of sit there instead.
Did something stressful happen in your life around the time these symptoms started?

Yeah… I guess it did kind of line up with work. It’s been about three weeks, maybe a little more, since the casino reorganized all the security stuff and changed what I’m assigned to.

And I know jobs change, right, like that’s not some huge life tragedy or anything… but the whole setup got shuffled. Different posts, different expectations, people acting like they know how surveillance should run when they’ve barely sat in the room— sorry, that’s probably beside the point.

But yeah, around then is when I started feeling off.
Have you been feeling hopeless?

I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless exactly… but most days there’s this heavy, flat feeling I’m carrying around. Like I can be at home with my family, or sitting in the break room while people are talking, and I’m there, but I’m not really there.

It’s weird, because everybody else seems like they’re just going through the day normally, and I’m kind of off to the side in my own head. Not thinking some big dramatic thing, just… flat. Heavy.
How have you been sleeping lately?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I sleep, but I haven’t been keeping track of it or anything.

Some nights I’m just kind of… in bed, and I couldn’t tell you if it’s normal or not. My wife would probably have a better sense, honestly—she notices stuff like if I’m tossing around, but I don’t know. I haven’t really paid attention to it the way I probably should.
Have you been eating less because you’re worried about your weight or how your body looks?

No, not really because of weight or how I look. I mean, I’m not thrilled with getting older and the whole… belt feeling tighter after sitting all shift thing, but that’s not why.

It’s more like I just don’t want food. I came in partly because the last few weeks I’ll get off a shift and even stuff I normally like just sits there in front of me. I take a few bites because I know I should, or because someone’s watching, but it’s like forcing it down. Then I’m done.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I mean… I’m not sitting there making a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. It’s not like that.

But, yeah… sometimes I catch myself thinking if I just didn’t wake up, maybe that wouldn’t be the worst thing. Like I wouldn’t have to keep getting up and pushing through the same heaviness. And then I feel weird even saying that out loud, because I know how it sounds. I’m not trying to scare anybody. It’s just… the thought shows up.
Have you been feeling this down nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. Most days it’s there, that kind of heavy, flat feeling. Like I can be at home with my family, or sitting in the break room at work while people are talking about whatever game was on, and I’m there, but I’m not really… there.

I don’t know if it’s every single day, because some days all kind of blur together, especially with shift work, but it’s been going on enough that it feels like most days lately.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?

I don’t know… tired compared to what, I guess? My schedule’s always kind of weird, so I’m used to feeling worn out sometimes.

Lately I wouldn’t say I’ve been, like, collapsing or anything. I still get through what I have to do. Some days I do feel drained, but then again a lot of people at work say the same thing—standing around watching monitors all night will do that to you. So… I’m not sure if it’s unusual, exactly.
Have you been having more trouble concentrating lately?

Yeah… I guess so. It’s mostly at work that I notice it. Like when I’m watching the CCTV feeds, I’ll realize my mind’s wandered off and I missed what I was supposed to be paying attention to.

And with incident reports, too—I’ll write something up and then have to read the same line over and over because it’s not sticking. Which is frustrating, because I’ve done that job long enough that I don’t usually make dumb mistakes like that. Lately I have, though. Even little stuff I should’ve caught.
Have these feelings been making it harder for you to do your job or take care of things at home?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still showing up. I’m not calling out or anything, and the basics at home are getting done, like bills and taking trash out—well, most of that.

But at work it’s starting to show, I think. I messed up some documentation, like little details in reports that I normally wouldn’t miss. And there was a surveillance thing I should’ve caught sooner. It’s funny, because they train you to stare at screens for hours and notice one tiny thing out of place, but lately my head just kind of… drifts.

Anyway, I got a formal warning over it, which hasn’t really happened to me before. So yeah, I guess it is making the job harder in a way it didn’t used to.
When you’re away from work, do you still feel this heavy, flat mood?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not just work. I mean, work makes it obvious because there’s stuff I’m supposed to be watching, but even when I’m home, it’s kind of still there.

Like I’ll be sitting with my family, or even just in the break room before a shift, and I feel… flat, I guess. Heavy. Not crying or anything dramatic, just like I’m there but not really there. Sometimes the TV’s on or people are talking and I’m just sort of… carrying it around with me.
Have you been moving or talking noticeably more slowly than usual lately?

Yeah… I think people at work have noticed that. Like in briefings, I’m not exactly dragging my feet, but I’m slower getting moving, and when somebody asks me something it takes me a second too long to answer.

It’s strange, because briefings are usually quick—same room, same radios, somebody always making some dumb joke about the coffee—and lately I’ll be standing there feeling like my body and my mouth are both a step behind everybody else.
